steps: The equation wrapped $x$ in two layers: first "times 3", then "plus 5".
Unwrap backwards: peel off the "+5" (subtract 5), then peel off the "times 3" (divide by 3).
Inside the wrapping you find $x = 5$.

prompt: Four friends split a pizza bill equally, and each friend pays $\$7$. Solve $\frac{b}{4} = 7$ to find the whole bill $b$ in dollars. Give just the number.
hint: The bill was DIVIDED by $4$. Undo division with multiplication.

hints.text: The bill was DIVIDED by $4$. Undo division with multiplication.
Multiply BOTH sides by $4$: $b = 7 \times 4$.
$b = 28$. The bill was $\$28$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Collect the shares
steps: Each of the 4 friends puts $\$7$ on the table.
The pile is the whole bill: $7 + 7 + 7 + 7 = 28$ dollars.

prompt: Two concert tickets plus a $\$6$ service fee cost $\$96$ in total. Solve $2t + 6 = 96$ to find the price $t$ of one ticket in dollars. Give just the number.
hint: Take the fee off first: subtract $6$ from both sides.

hints.text: Take the fee off first: subtract $6$ from both sides.
$2t = 90$. Now divide both sides by $2$.
$t = 90 \div 2 = 45$ dollars.

alternativeExplanations.title: As a balance scale
steps: Left pan: two ticket-boxes and a $\$6$ weight. Right pan: $\$96$.
Lift the $\$6$ off each pan: two boxes balance $\$90$.
Split each pan in half: one box balances $\$45$.

prompt: Solve for $x$: $\frac{x}{3} - 2 = 4$. Give just the number.
hint: The $-2$ happened last, so undo it first: add $2$ to both sides.

hints.text: The $-2$ happened last, so undo it first: add $2$ to both sides.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Simpler version: $\frac{x}{3} = 4$ gives $x = 12$. Your problem just has a $-2$ to undo FIRST, before you multiply by $3$.
$\frac{x}{3} = 6$. Now undo the "divide by 3" by multiplying both sides by $3$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Unwrap the present
steps: $x$ got wrapped twice: first "divide by 3", then "minus 2".
Unwrap in reverse: add 2 back (get 6), then multiply by 3 (get 18).

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: Multiplying by 3 first gives x − 2 = 12 — but the −2 was never divided by 3, so that move breaks the equation.
Unwrap backwards: the last thing done to x was −2, so undo it first (x/3 = 6), THEN multiply by 3 to get 18.

prompt: You have $\$9$ saved and add $\$4.50$ to your jar every week. Solve $4.5w + 9 = 36$ to find how many weeks until you reach $\$36$. Give just the number.
hint: Subtract the $\$9$ head start from both sides first.

hints.text: Subtract the $\$9$ head start from both sides first.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try round numbers: if you added $\$9$ a week you would need $27 \div 9 = 3$ weeks. Same recipe here, just divide by $4.5$ instead.
$4.5w = 27$. Now divide both sides by $4.5$.
$w = 27 \div 4.5 = 6$ weeks.

alternativeExplanations.title: Think in half-dollars
steps: $\$4.50$ a week is 9 half-dollars a week, and you need $\$27$ more, which is 54 half-dollars.
$54 \div 9 = 6$ weeks — same answer, no decimals needed.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: Dividing 36 by 4.50 right away gives 8 weeks — it spends your $9 of savings twice.
The $9 was already in the jar, so subtract it first: 4.5w = 27, and w = 6. Fixed money first, weekly money second.

prompt: You start a video game with $30$ energy points and use $2$ points every round. Solve $30 - 2r = 18$ to find how many rounds $r$ you have played. Give just the number.
hint: Subtract $30$ from both sides first — watch the signs.

hints.text: Subtract $30$ from both sides first — watch the signs.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Simpler: $30 - 2r = 20$ means $2r = 10$, so $r = 5$. Yours works the same way — the energy SUBTRACTS each round.
$-2r = -12$. Divide both sides by $-2$.
$r = -12 \div -2 = 6$ rounds.

alternativeExplanations.title: Count what you spent
steps: You started at 30 points and now sit at 18, so you spent $30 - 18 = 12$ points.
At 2 points a round, that is $12 \div 2 = 6$ rounds.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: Stopping at 30 − 18 = 12 answers “how many points did I use?” — not “how many rounds?”
The 12 points still need to be turned into rounds: 12 ÷ 2 = 6. Word problems love to hide one last division.

prompt: Solve for $x$: $2x + 3x = 25$. Give just the number.
hint: First tidy up: $2x$ and $3x$ are like terms. Combine them.

hints.text: First tidy up: $2x$ and $3x$ are like terms. Combine them.
$2x + 3x = 5x$, so $5x = 25$. Now divide both sides by $5$.

explanation: Now solve $5x = 25$: divide both sides by 5.

alternativeExplanations.title: Count the boxes
steps: 2 mystery boxes plus 3 more mystery boxes is 5 identical boxes.
Five boxes together weigh 25, so each box weighs $25 \div 5 = 5$.

prompt: Solve for $x$: $3(x + 2) = 21$. Give just the number.
hint: Distribute: the $3$ outside hands itself to EVERYONE inside the parentheses.

hints.text: Distribute: the $3$ outside hands itself to EVERYONE inside the parentheses.
$3x + 6 = 21$. Subtract $6$, then divide by $3$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Divide first instead
steps: Both sides can be divided by 3 right away: $x + 2 = 7$.
Subtract 2: $x = 5$. Two roads, same answer.

prompt: Solve for $x$: $5x = 2x + 12$. Give just the number.
hint: Get all the $x$'s on one team: subtract $2x$ from both sides.

hints.text: Get all the $x$'s on one team: subtract $2x$ from both sides.

alternativeExplanations.title: As a balance scale
steps: Left pan: 5 boxes. Right pan: 2 boxes plus a 12-gram weight.
Lift 2 boxes off EACH pan: 3 boxes balance 12 grams.
Each box is $12 \div 3 = 4$ grams.

prompt: A party room costs $\$40$ to rent plus $\$6$ per guest, and your whole budget is $\$100$. Solve $40 + 6g = 100$ to find how many guests $g$ you can invite. Give just the number.
hint: The room fee is one-time. Subtract $40$ from both sides first.

hints.text: The room fee is one-time. Subtract $40$ from both sides first.
$6g = 60$. Divide both sides by $6$.
$g = 60 \div 6 = 10$ guests.

alternativeExplanations.title: Budget leftovers
steps: Pay the room first: $\$100 - \$40$ leaves $\$60$ for guests.
Each guest costs $\$6$, so $60 \div 6 = 10$ guests fit the budget.

prompt: You hand $3$ snacks to every person at a table of $g$ guests plus $4$ helpers, using $33$ snacks in all. Solve $3(g + 4) = 33$ to find the number of guests $g$. Give just the number.
hint: Distribute: the $3$ snacks go to EVERYONE inside the parentheses — guests AND helpers.

hints.text: Distribute: the $3$ snacks go to EVERYONE inside the parentheses — guests AND helpers.
$3g + 12 = 33$. Subtract $12$ from both sides.
$3g = 21$, so $g = 7$ guests.

alternativeExplanations.title: Count heads first
steps: 33 snacks at 3 per person means $33 \div 3 = 11$ people got snacks.
4 of them are helpers, so $11 - 4 = 7$ are guests.

prompt: Phone plan A costs $\$12$ plus $\$0.10$ per minute. Plan B costs $\$0.30$ per minute with no base fee. Solve $12 + 0.10m = 0.30m$ to find the number of minutes $m$ where the plans cost the same. Give just the number.
hint: Get the $m$'s on one team: subtract $0.10m$ from both sides.

hints.text: Get the $m$'s on one team: subtract $0.10m$ from both sides.
$12 = 0.20m$. Divide both sides by $0.20$.
$m = 12 \div 0.20 = 60$ minutes.

explanation: Check: plan A costs $12 + 0.10(60) = \$18$; plan B costs $0.30(60) = \$18$. ✓ Same price at 60 minutes.

alternativeExplanations.title: Race with a head start
steps: Plan B charges 20 cents more per minute, but plan A starts $\$12$ ahead.
B catches up 20 cents each minute. To close a $\$12$ gap takes $1200 \div 20 = 60$ minutes.

prompt: Solve for $x$: $7x - 4 = 3x + 16$. Give just the number.
hint: Move all the $x$'s to one team first: subtract $3x$ from both sides.

hints.text: Move all the $x$'s to one team first: subtract $3x$ from both sides.
$4x - 4 = 16$. Now add $4$ to both sides.

alternativeExplanations.title: As a balance scale
steps: Left pan: 7 boxes with 4 grams removed. Right pan: 3 boxes plus 16 grams.
Lift 3 boxes off each pan, then add 4 grams to each pan: 4 boxes balance 20 grams.
Each box is 5 grams.

prompt: Hall A charges $\$40$ plus $\$6$ per guest. Hall B charges $\$10$ per guest with no rental fee. Solve $40 + 6g = 10g$ to find the number of guests $g$ where the two halls cost the same. Give just the number.
hint: Put the $g$'s on one team: subtract $6g$ from both sides.

hints.text: Put the $g$'s on one team: subtract $6g$ from both sides.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Test one guest count: at $5$ guests, Hall A costs $40 + 30 = 70$ and Hall B costs $50$. Keep testing, or set the two costs equal.
$40 = 4g$. Divide both sides by $4$.
$g = 40 \div 4 = 10$ guests.

explanation: Check: hall A costs $40 + 6(10) = \$100$; hall B costs $10(10) = \$100$. ✓

alternativeExplanations.title: Close the gap
steps: Hall B costs $\$4$ more per guest, but hall A starts with a $\$40$ fee.
Every guest closes the gap by $\$4$, so it takes $40 \div 4 = 10$ guests to tie.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: Giving Hall B a $40 fee too — writing 40 + 6g = 40 + 10g — makes the halls tie forever.
Each hall keeps its own rule: A is 40 + 6g, B is just 10g. Set THOSE equal, and g = 10 falls out.

prompt: Solve for $x$: $4(x - 2) = 2x + 6$. Give just the number.
hint: Distribute first: hand the $4$ to both terms inside the parentheses.

hints.text: Distribute first: hand the $4$ to both terms inside the parentheses.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Simpler: $4(x - 2) = 8$ gives $x - 2 = 2$, so $x = 4$. Yours adds x-terms on the right, so distribute first, then gather the x-terms.
$4x - 8 = 2x + 6$. Subtract $2x$ from both sides, then add $8$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Guess-and-check table
steps: Try $x = 5$: left is $4(3) = 12$, right is $16$ — right side wins.
Try $x = 7$: left is $4(5) = 20$, right is $20$ — they tie!
The table shows the sides meet exactly at $x = 7$.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: Writing 4(x − 2) as 4x − 2 forgets to hand the 4 to the second guest in the parentheses.
The outside number multiplies EVERYTHING inside: 4x − 8. Then 4x − 8 = 2x + 6 gives x = 7.

prompt: Solve for $x$: $5(x - 1) - 2x = 2x + 7$. Give just the number.
hint: Do the full cleanup routine: distribute the $5$, then combine like terms on the left.

hints.text: Do the full cleanup routine: distribute the $5$, then combine like terms on the left.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up by distributing only: $5(x - 1)$ is $5x - 5$. Now the left side is $5x - 5 - 2x = 3x - 5$. Much friendlier!
$5x - 5 - 2x = 3x - 5$, so the equation is $3x - 5 = 2x + 7$. Subtract $2x$ from both sides.

explanation: Combine like terms on the left: $5x - 5 - 2x = 3x - 5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Tidy each room first
steps: Treat each side like a messy room: you cannot compare them until both are tidy.
Left room tidied: $3x - 5$. Right room is already tidy: $2x + 7$.
Now the equation $3x - 5 = 2x + 7$ is a simple both-sides problem: $x = 12$.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: Rushing to move terms across before tidying loses the −5: mixing 5x − 1 − 2x is where this one goes wrong.
Clean your own side first: 5(x − 1) − 2x = 3x − 5. Only THEN cross the river: 3x − 5 = 2x + 7 gives x = 12.

prompt: Solve the inequality $x + 5 > 9$. Write your answer like "x > 4".
hint: Solve it just like an equation: undo the $+5$ on both sides.

hints.text: Solve it just like an equation: undo the $+5$ on both sides.

explanation: Subtract 5 from both sides, just like an equation.
Any number bigger than 4 works: try $x = 5$, since $5 + 5 = 10 > 9$. ✓

alternativeExplanations.title: On a number line
steps: Picture a number line with an OPEN dot at 4 (4 itself is not included).
Shade everything to the right — those are all the numbers whose "+5" beats 9.

prompt: A school bus holds at most $40$ students. Write an inequality for the number of students $s$ that can ride. Write it like "s <= 40".
hint: "At most 40" means 40 is the ceiling: 40 is OK, 41 is not.

hints.text: "At most 40" means 40 is the ceiling: 40 is OK, 41 is not.
So $s$ can be less than 40 OR equal to 40. Which symbol says that?
$s \le 40$ — written as "s <= 40".

explanation: "At most 40" means the count can be 40 or anything smaller.
The "or equal" bar matters: exactly 40 students is still allowed.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test the boundary
steps: Can 40 students ride? Yes — "at most 40" allows exactly 40.
Can 41 ride? No.
An inequality that says yes to 40 and no to 41 must be $s \le 40$.

prompt: Solve the inequality $x - 3 \ge 2$. Write your answer like "x >= 5".
hint: Undo the $-3$: add $3$ to both sides. The $\ge$ sign stays put.

hints.text: Undo the $-3$: add $3$ to both sides. The $\ge$ sign stays put.

explanation: Check the boundary: $5 - 3 = 2$, and $2 \ge 2$ is true, so 5 itself is included.

alternativeExplanations.title: On a number line
steps: Draw a CLOSED (filled) dot at 5, because $x = 5$ works.
Shade to the right: every number from 5 and up passes the test.

prompt: Solve the inequality $2x + 1 < 9$. Write your answer like "x < 4".
hint: Two steps, same as an equation: subtract $1$ from both sides first.

hints.text: Two steps, same as an equation: subtract $1$ from both sides first.
$2x < 8$. Divide both sides by $2$ — dividing by a POSITIVE keeps the sign as is.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test numbers like a detective
steps: Try $x = 4$: $2(4) + 1 = 9$, and $9 < 9$ is FALSE — so 4 is out.
Try $x = 3$: $7 < 9$ is true. Everything below 4 works: $x < 4$.

prompt: You have a $\$25$ budget and each game credit costs $\$4$. Using $4c \le 25$, what is the greatest number of whole credits $c$ you can buy? Give just the number.
hint: Divide both sides by $4$: $c \le 25 \div 4$.

hints.text: Divide both sides by $4$: $c \le 25 \div 4$.
$c \le 6.25$. You cannot buy a quarter of a credit — round DOWN to a whole number.
The greatest whole number of credits is $6$.

explanation: Credits come in whole numbers, so take the biggest whole number that fits: 6.

alternativeExplanations.title: Spend it out loud
steps: Count by 4s until you would pass 25: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24 — that is 6 credits for $\$24$.
A 7th credit needs $\$28$, which is more than $\$25$. Stop at 6.

prompt: Solve the inequality $-3x > 12$. Write your answer like "x < -4".
hint: To get $x$ alone, divide both sides by $-3$. Dividing by a NEGATIVE flips the sign.

hints.text: To get $x$ alone, divide both sides by $-3$. Dividing by a NEGATIVE flips the sign.
$x \; ? \; 12 \div (-3)$ — the $>$ turns into $<$.

explanation: Divide both sides by $-3$ and FLIP the inequality: $x < -4$.
Dividing by a negative is like walking backwards — it turns you around.

alternativeExplanations.title: See why the flip is real
steps: Start with a true fact: $2 < 6$.
Multiply both sides by $-1$: you get $-2$ and $-6$, and now $-2 > -6$.
Negatives reverse the order on the number line, so the sign MUST flip.

prompt: You need at least $\$50$ for a class trip. You have $\$18$ and save $\$8$ each week. Using $8w + 18 \ge 50$, what is the fewest number of whole weeks $w$ you must save? Give just the number.
hint: Subtract $18$ from both sides first.

hints.text: Subtract $18$ from both sides first.
$8w \ge 32$. Divide both sides by $8$.
$w \ge 4$, so the fewest whole weeks is $4$.

explanation: The fewest whole weeks is 4. Check: $8(4) + 18 = \$50$, and "at least $\$50$" includes exactly $\$50$. ✓

alternativeExplanations.title: Track the jar week by week
steps: Week 4 is the first time the jar reaches $\$50$, so 4 weeks is the fewest.

prompt: Solve the inequality $5 - 2x \le 11$. Write your answer like "x >= -3".
hint: Subtract $5$ from both sides first — the sign does not flip for subtraction.

hints.text: Subtract $5$ from both sides first — the sign does not flip for subtraction.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Practice the flip on a tiny one: $-2x \le 6$ gives $x \ge -3$ — dividing by a NEGATIVE flips the sign.
$-2x \le 6$. Now divide by $-2$ and FLIP the sign.

explanation: Divide both sides by $-2$ and flip $\le$ to $\ge$: $x \ge -3$.
Check: $x = 0$ gives $5 - 0 = 5 \le 11$ ✓, and $x = -4$ gives $5 + 8 = 13$, which fails — so the cut really is at $-3$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Dodge the flip entirely
steps: Add $2x$ to both sides instead: $5 \le 11 + 2x$.
Subtract 11: $-6 \le 2x$. Divide by positive 2: $-3 \le x$.
Same answer, $x \ge -3$, and you never divided by a negative.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: x ≤ −3 is the no-flip answer, and it fails the smell test: try x = −10 and 5 − 2(−10) = 25, which is NOT ≤ 11.
You divided by −2, so the sign flips: x ≥ −3. One test number always exposes a missing flip.

prompt: A bus holds at most $40$ students. $12$ students are already aboard, and the rest arrive in groups of $4$. Using $12 + 4g \le 40$, what is the greatest number of whole groups $g$ that can still board? Give just the number.
hint: Subtract the $12$ students already aboard from both sides.

hints.text: Subtract the $12$ students already aboard from both sides.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a smaller bus: if it holds $20$ and $12$ are aboard, only $8$ seats remain. Find the leftover seats first, then split them into groups.
$4g \le 28$. Divide both sides by $4$.
$g \le 7$, so at most $7$ groups can board.

explanation: The greatest whole number of groups is 7. Check: $12 + 4(7) = 40$ students — exactly full, and "at most 40" allows it. ✓

alternativeExplanations.title: Count the empty seats
steps: The bus has $40 - 12 = 28$ empty seats.
Each group fills 4 seats, so $28 \div 4 = 7$ groups fit exactly.
An 8th group would need 4 more seats than the bus has.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: 40 ÷ 4 = 10 groups forgets the 12 students already in their seats.
Seats left: 40 − 12 = 28. Then 28 ÷ 4 = 7 groups. Subtract what is used before dividing what is left.

prompt: Solve the inequality $-4x + 3 < 23$. Write your answer like "x > -5".
hint: Subtract $3$ from both sides first: $-4x < 20$.

hints.text: Subtract $3$ from both sides first: $-4x < 20$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Simpler: $-4x < 8$ gives $x > -2$ (sign flips!). Yours just needs the $+3$ moved over first.
Now divide by $-4$. Dividing by a negative FLIPS the sign: $<$ becomes $>$.

explanation: Divide both sides by $-4$ and flip $<$ to $>$: $x > -5$.
Check: $x = 0$ gives $3 < 23$ ✓, and $x = -6$ gives $24 + 3 = 27$, which is not $< 23$ — the boundary is $-5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: On a number line
steps: Put an OPEN dot at $-5$, since $-5$ itself gives $23 < 23$, which is false.
Shade to the right: every number bigger than $-5$ makes the left side smaller than 23.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: x < −5 keeps the sign pointing the old way after dividing by −4 — the classic missing flip.
Check with x = 0: −4(0) + 3 = 3 < 23 ✓, so 0 must be in the answer. Only x > −5 contains 0.

prompt: A function machine DOUBLES every input. You feed it a $7$. What number comes out?
hint: A function is a machine: one input goes in, one output comes out.

hints.text: A function is a machine: one input goes in, one output comes out.
The machine's rule is "double" — multiply the input by $2$.

explanation: The machine's rule: multiply the input by $2$.
One input in, exactly ONE output out — that is what makes it a function.

alternativeExplanations.title: As a table
steps: Build an input-output table: $1 \to 2$, $2 \to 4$, $3 \to 6$.
Every output is twice its input, so $7 \to 14$.

prompt: On a quiz, each question is worth $4$ points, so your score is $f(q) = 4q$. What is $f(3)$? Give just the number.
hint: $f(3)$ means "feed the machine a $3$" — replace $q$ with $3$.

hints.text: $f(3)$ means "feed the machine a $3$" — replace $q$ with $3$.
$4 \times 3 = 12$ points.

explanation: $f(q) = 4q$ is a machine named $f$: input questions, output points.

alternativeExplanations.title: Count it out
steps: Each question is worth $4$ points.
Three questions: $4 + 4 + 4 = 12$ points.

prompt: A function's table shows: input $1 \to$ output $5$, input $2 \to$ output $10$, input $3 \to$ output $15$. What is the output for input $2$?
hint: Find the row of the table where the input is $2$.

hints.text: Find the row of the table where the input is $2$.
The table pairs each input with exactly one output: $2 \to ?$
Input $2$ pairs with output $10$.

explanation: A table is a list of the machine's input-output pairs.

alternativeExplanations.title: Spot the rule
steps: Each output is $5$ times its input: $1 \to 5$, $3 \to 15$.
So input $2$ gives $2 \times 5 = 10$.

prompt: Let $f(x) = 3x + 2$. What is $f(4)$? Give just the number.
hint: $f(4)$ means feed the machine a $4$: replace every $x$ with $4$.

hints.text: $f(4)$ means feed the machine a $4$: replace every $x$ with $4$.
Compute $3 \times 4$ first, then add $2$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Two-step machine
steps: Picture the machine doing two moves: first "times 3", then "plus 2".
Input $4$: times $3$ gives $12$; plus $2$ gives $14$.

prompt: Let $g(x) = 10 - 2x$. What is $g(3)$? Give just the number.
hint: $g$ is just another machine's name. Feed it a $3$: replace $x$ with $3$.

hints.text: $g$ is just another machine's name. Feed it a $3$: replace $x$ with $3$.
Compute $2 \times 3$ first, then subtract from $10$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Countdown machine
steps: The machine starts at $10$ and takes away $2$ for every $1$ of input.
Input $3$: take away $2$ three times — $10 \to 8 \to 6 \to 4$.

prompt: A photo filter on your phone is a function: it adds $15$ to a photo's brightness, $f(p) = p + 15$. A photo has brightness $40$. What brightness comes out?
hint: The filter is a machine: one photo in, exactly one filtered photo out.

hints.text: The filter is a machine: one photo in, exactly one filtered photo out.

explanation: The filter's rule: add $15$ to the brightness.
Every input photo gets exactly ONE output photo — that is why a filter is a function.

alternativeExplanations.title: Table of photos
steps: Try a few inputs: brightness $10 \to 25$, $20 \to 35$, $30 \to 45$.
Every output is $15$ more, so $40 \to 55$.

prompt: A vending machine only has buttons numbered $1$ through $8$ — those are its allowed inputs (its DOMAIN). What is the largest number in the domain?
hint: Domain = the set of inputs the machine ACCEPTS.

hints.text: Domain = the set of inputs the machine ACCEPTS.
The buttons run from $1$ up to $8$. Which is the biggest allowed input?
The largest allowed input is $8$.

explanation: The domain is the list of allowed inputs: the buttons $1, 2, 3, \ldots, 8$.
Pressing $9$ does nothing — $9$ is not in the domain.
The largest number in the domain is $8$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Domain vs range
steps: Inputs (buttons) form the domain; outputs (snacks) form the range.
The question asks about buttons only, and they stop at $8$.

prompt: Let $f(x) = 5x$. If $f(x) = 35$, what input $x$ was fed into the machine?
hint: This time you know the OUTPUT ($35$) and need the input. Run the machine backward.

hints.text: This time you know the OUTPUT ($35$) and need the input. Run the machine backward.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Easier machine: if $f(x) = 5x$ and the output is $10$, the input was $10 \div 5 = 2$. Undo the machine by dividing.
The machine multiplies by $5$, so undo it: divide $35$ by $5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Guess and check
steps: Try inputs: $f(6) = 30$ — too small. $f(8) = 40$ — too big.
$f(7) = 35$ — exactly right, so the input was $7$.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: Feeding 35 INTO the machine — 5 × 35 = 175 — answers the reverse of what was asked.
35 is what came OUT. To find what went in, undo the machine: 35 ÷ 5 = 7.

prompt: Your quiz score is $f(q) = 4q$ points, and the quiz has at most $10$ questions ($q$ can be $0$ to $10$). What is the LARGEST output in the range?
hint: Range = the set of possible OUTPUTS. The biggest output comes from the biggest input.

hints.text: Range = the set of possible OUTPUTS. The biggest output comes from the biggest input.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Check the ends: $q = 0$ gives $0$ points and $q = 10$ gives $40$ points. The range is everything the machine CAN output between those.
The biggest allowed input is $q = 10$. Compute $f(10)$.

explanation: The rule multiplies by $4$, so bigger inputs give bigger outputs.

alternativeExplanations.title: List the outputs
steps: The outputs are $0, 4, 8, 12, \ldots$ climbing by $4$ each time.
They stop when the questions run out at $q = 10$: the last one is $40$.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: Answering 10 hands back the number of questions — the input — when the question wants the best possible SCORE.
Push the biggest allowed input through the machine: f(10) = 4 × 10 = 40 points.

prompt: Let $f(x) = 2x + 3$. The machine spits out $19$. What input went in?
hint: The machine does "times $2$, then plus $3$". Undo the steps in REVERSE order.

hints.text: The machine does "times $2$, then plus $3$". Undo the steps in REVERSE order.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Simpler: $2x + 3 = 9$ gives $2x = 6$, so $x = 3$. Undo in reverse — subtract the $3$, then divide by the $2$.
First undo "plus $3$": $19 - 3 = 16$. Then undo "times $2$".

alternativeExplanations.title: Check with the table
steps: Try $f(7) = 17$ and $f(9) = 21$ — the output $19$ sits between them.
$f(8) = 2 \times 8 + 3 = 19$. The input was $8$.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: Running 19 forward — 2(19) + 3 = 41 — uses the machine in the wrong direction.
Walk backwards through the machine, last step first: 19 − 3 = 16, then 16 ÷ 2 = 8.

prompt: A staircase rises $6$ units while running $2$ units across. What is the slope (rise over run)?
hint: Slope = rise $\div$ run.

hints.text: Slope = rise $\div$ run.
Rise is $6$, run is $2$: compute $6 \div 2$.

explanation: For every $1$ step across, the stairs climb $3$ up.

alternativeExplanations.title: Shrink the staircase
steps: $6$ up over $2$ across is the same steepness as $3$ up over $1$ across.
The "up per one across" number IS the slope: $3$.

prompt: Your phone battery drops from $80\%$ to $56\%$ in $2$ hours. How many percent does it drop per hour?
hint: First find the TOTAL drop: $80 - 56$.

hints.text: First find the TOTAL drop: $80 - 56$.
It dropped $24\%$ in $2$ hours. Divide by the hours.
$24 \div 2 = 12$ percent per hour.

explanation: The rate of change is $-12\%$ per hour — battery is going DOWN.

alternativeExplanations.title: As stairs going down
steps: Picture a staircase: every 1 hour across (run), the battery steps 12 down (rise = −12).
Slope = rise over run = −24 over 2 = −12 per hour.

prompt: A wheelchair ramp rises $2$ ft over a run of $8$ ft. What is its slope? Write it as a fraction.
hint: Slope = rise over run: put $2$ over $8$.

hints.text: Slope = rise over run: put $2$ over $8$.
$\frac{2}{8}$ can be simplified — divide top and bottom by $2$.

explanation: The ramp climbs $1$ ft for every $4$ ft across — a gentle slope.

alternativeExplanations.title: One foot at a time
steps: The ramp gains $2$ ft of height spread over $8$ ft of floor.
Per single foot across: $2 \div 8 = 0.25$ ft up — that decimal equals $\frac{1}{4}$.

prompt: Find the slope of the line through $(1, 2)$ and $(3, 8)$.
hint: Slope $= \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$ — change in $y$ over change in $x$.

hints.text: Slope $= \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$ — change in $y$ over change in $x$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Walk the stairs
steps: Start at $(1, 2)$. To reach $(3, 8)$ you walk $2$ across and $6$ up.
Per single step across that is $3$ up — slope $3$.

prompt: Find the slope of the line through $(0, 10)$ and $(5, 0)$.
hint: The line goes DOWN from left to right, so expect a negative slope.

hints.text: The line goes DOWN from left to right, so expect a negative slope.

alternativeExplanations.title: Downhill stairs
steps: From $(0,10)$ to $(5,0)$ you drop $10$ while walking $5$ across.
Each step across drops you $2$: the slope is $-2$.

prompt: You walk dogs for pay. After $3$ walks you have earned $\$18$; after $5$ walks, $\$30$. What is your rate in dollars per walk?
hint: Rate = change in money $\div$ change in walks — that is a slope!

hints.text: Rate = change in money $\div$ change in walks — that is a slope!
Money changed $30 - 18 = 12$ dollars over $5 - 3 = 2$ walks.
$12 \div 2 = 6$ dollars per walk.

explanation: Treat the data as points: $(3, 18)$ and $(5, 30)$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check with one point
steps: If each walk pays $\$6$, then $3$ walks pay $3 \times 6 = \$18$. Matches!
And $5$ walks pay $5 \times 6 = \$30$. The rate $\$6$ per walk fits both.

prompt: Find the slope of the line through $(2, 1)$ and $(6, 4)$. Write it as a fraction.
hint: Slope $= \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$. Keep the answer as a fraction.

hints.text: Slope $= \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$. Keep the answer as a fraction.
Slope $= \frac{3}{4}$.

explanation: Slope $= \frac{3}{4}$ — up $3$ for every $4$ across. A slope does not have to be a whole number!

alternativeExplanations.title: Gentle stairs
steps: From $(2,1)$ walk $4$ tiles across and climb only $3$ up to land on $(6,4)$.
Less than $1$ up per tile across: exactly $\frac{3}{4}$ up each tile.

prompt: Find the slope of the line through $(4, 7)$ and $(9, 7)$.
hint: Compare the $y$-values of the two points. Do they change at all?

hints.text: Compare the $y$-values of the two points. Do they change at all?

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Plot two points with the SAME height, like $(1, 5)$ and $(6, 5)$. The line is flat, so it rises $0$ — and $0$ divided by anything is $0$.
Rise: $7 - 7 = 0$. Run: $9 - 4 = 5$. Now divide.
$0 \div 5 = 0$. A flat line has slope $0$.

explanation: Slope $= \frac{0}{5} = 0$: a perfectly FLAT line, like a hallway floor.

alternativeExplanations.title: Flat floor, not no floor
steps: Both points sit at height $7$, so walking between them is walking on flat ground.
Flat means zero steepness — slope $0$ (not "no slope").

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: “Undefined” is the trap word here — that is the VERTICAL line's slope, not the flat line's.
Both points sit at height 7, so the rise is 0, and 0 ÷ 5 = 0. Flat road, zero steepness — a real number.

prompt: A battery log on your phone reads: hour $1 \to 88\%$, hour $3 \to 64\%$. What is the rate of change in percent per hour? (Include the sign.)
hint: The battery is DRAINING, so the rate should come out negative.

hints.text: The battery is DRAINING, so the rate should come out negative.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Simpler log: $80\%$ at hour $1$ and $70\%$ at hour $2$ drops $10$ over $1$ hour = $-10$ per hour. Find the drop, then divide by the hours.
Change in percent: $64 - 88 = -24$. Change in hours: $3 - 1 = 2$.
$-24 \div 2 = -12$ percent per hour.

explanation: Slope $= \frac{-24}{2} = -12$: the battery loses $12\%$ each hour.

alternativeExplanations.title: Fill the missing hour
steps: From hour $1$ to hour $3$ the battery fell $24\%$ over $2$ hours — split it evenly.
Hour $2$ must read $76\%$: each hour drops $12$, so the rate is $-12$.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: Dividing by 3 — the hour on the clock — instead of the 2-hour GAP gives −8, a neat wrong answer.
Slope uses the change in time, not the time itself: from hour 1 to hour 3 is 2 hours. −24 ÷ 2 = −12% per hour.

prompt: Find the slope of the line through $(1, 5)$ and $(5, 2)$. Write it as a fraction.
hint: The $y$-values drop from $5$ to $2$, so the slope is negative.

hints.text: The $y$-values drop from $5$ to $2$, so the slope is negative.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with $(1, 5)$ and $(3, 1)$: rise $= 1 - 5 = -4$, run $= 3 - 1 = 2$, slope $= -2$. Same subtraction order every time.
Slope $= \frac{-3}{4}$.

explanation: Slope $= -\frac{3}{4}$ — a gentle downhill: down $3$ for every $4$ across.

alternativeExplanations.title: Subtract the other way
steps: Swap the order of BOTH subtractions: rise $5 - 2 = 3$, run $1 - 5 = -4$.
$\frac{3}{-4}$ is still $-\frac{3}{4}$ — same slope, as long as both are swapped together.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: Flipping to run-over-rise gives −4/3 — right numbers, upside-down fraction.
Rise first, run second: (2 − 5) on top, (5 − 1) on the bottom → −3/4. Say “rise over run” as you write it.

prompt: In the equation $y = 5x + 2$, what is the slope?
hint: In $y = mx + b$, the slope $m$ is the number MULTIPLYING $x$.

hints.text: In $y = mx + b$, the slope $m$ is the number MULTIPLYING $x$.
What number sits right in front of $x$ in $5x + 2$?
The slope is $5$.

explanation: The number multiplying $x$ is $m = 5$ — how you MOVE.
The $+2$ is $b$, where you START — not the slope.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test two inputs
steps: One step across made $y$ jump by $5$ — that jump is the slope.

prompt: In the equation $y = 3x - 4$, what is the $y$-intercept?
hint: In $y = mx + b$, the $y$-intercept $b$ is the number ADDED at the end — where the line STARTS on the $y$-axis.

hints.text: In $y = mx + b$, the $y$-intercept $b$ is the number ADDED at the end — where the line STARTS on the $y$-axis.
$3x - 4$ is the same as $3x + (-4)$.
The $y$-intercept is $-4$.

explanation: The minus sign belongs to the $4$ — the start is BELOW zero.

alternativeExplanations.title: Plug in x = 0
steps: The $y$-intercept is the $y$-value when $x = 0$.

prompt: A scooter app charges $y = 2 + 0.15m$ dollars for a ride of $m$ minutes. How many dollars do you pay before riding a single minute ($m = 0$)?
hint: Before riding, $m = 0$. That makes this a "where do you START" question.

hints.text: Before riding, $m = 0$. That makes this a "where do you START" question.
Plug in $m = 0$: $y = 2 + 0.15 \times 0$.
$y = 2 + 0 = 2$ dollars — the unlock fee.

explanation: The $2$ is the $y$-intercept $b$ — the START, the unlock fee you pay no matter what.
The $0.15$ is the slope — how the cost MOVES per minute.

alternativeExplanations.title: Start-then-move
steps: Every $y = mx + b$ story splits into a start and a move.
Here the start is $\$2$ (unlock) and the move is $\$0.15$ each minute; at zero minutes only the start is charged.

prompt: A plant is $4$ cm tall and grows $3$ cm each week: $h = 4 + 3w$. How tall is it after $5$ weeks?
hint: Start at $4$ (that is $b$), then MOVE up $3$ for each of the $5$ weeks.

hints.text: Start at $4$ (that is $b$), then MOVE up $3$ for each of the $5$ weeks.
Growth: $3 \times 5 = 15$. Add the starting height.

alternativeExplanations.title: Week by week
steps: Start $4$, then climb $3$ each week: $7, 10, 13, 16, 19$.
After week $5$ the plant is $19$ cm — same as $4 + 3 \times 5$.

prompt: A line has equation $y = 2x + 1$. What is $y$ when $x = 4$?
hint: Replace $x$ with $4$ in the equation.

hints.text: Replace $x$ with $4$ in the equation.
$y = 2 \times 4 + 1$. Multiply first.

explanation: So the point $(4, 9)$ sits on the line.

alternativeExplanations.title: Start, then climb
steps: Start at $b = 1$ on the $y$-axis.
Slope $2$ means climb $2$ per step across; four steps climb $8$: $1 + 8 = 9$.

prompt: Your savings follow $s = 15 + 5w$: you start with $\$15$ and add $\$5$ each week. How many dollars do you have after $6$ weeks?
hint: START at $15$, then MOVE up $5$ per week for $6$ weeks.

hints.text: START at $15$, then MOVE up $5$ per week for $6$ weeks.
Added money: $5 \times 6 = 30$. Now add the start.

alternativeExplanations.title: On the graph
steps: The savings line starts at $(0, 15)$ and rises $5$ for every $1$ week across.
Six steps of rise $5$ lift you $30$ above the start: $15 + 30 = 45$.

prompt: A line has equation $y = 3$. What is $y$ on this line when $x = 100$?
hint: $y = 3$ has no $x$ in it at all. What does that tell you?

hints.text: $y = 3$ has no $x$ in it at all. What does that tell you?
Think of it as $y = 0x + 3$: slope $0$, start $3$.
$y$ is ALWAYS $3$, even at $x = 100$.

explanation: With zero slope the line never climbs or falls — it is horizontal.

alternativeExplanations.title: A flat hallway
steps: Start at height $3$ and move with slope $0$: every step across stays at height $3$.
Walk $100$ steps and you are still at height $3$.

prompt: The scooter app charges $y = 2 + 0.15m$ dollars for $m$ minutes. How many dollars does a $20$-minute ride cost?
hint: Plug in $m = 20$. Handle $0.15 \times 20$ carefully.

hints.text: Plug in $m = 20$. Handle $0.15 \times 20$ carefully.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try $10$ minutes first: $2 + 0.15(10) = 2 + 1.50 = \$3.50$. Now do the same with $20$ minutes.
$0.15 \times 20 = 3$. Now add the unlock fee.
$2 + 3 = 5$ dollars.

alternativeExplanations.title: Money in pieces
steps: Ten minutes of riding costs $10 \times \$0.15 = \$1.50$, so twenty minutes costs $\$3$.
Add the $\$2$ unlock fee at the start: $\$5$ total.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: Stopping at 0.15 × 20 = 3 forgets the $2 unlock fee that every ride pays.
The rule has two parts: 2 + 0.15(20) = 2 + 3 = $5. Fixed fee plus the per-minute part, always both.

prompt: To graph $y = 3x + 2$, you plot the start $(0, 2)$, then move right $1$. What $y$-value do you land on?
hint: The slope $3$ means: for every $1$ right, go UP $3$.

hints.text: The slope $3$ means: for every $1$ right, go UP $3$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Start at the y-intercept $(0, 2)$. Moving right $1$ climbs by the slope $3$: $2 + 3 = 5$. The slope IS the step size.
Start at height $2$, rise $3$: $2 + 3 = ?$
You land at $(1, 5)$, so $y = 5$.

explanation: Graphing recipe: plot $b$, then use $m$ as rise over run.
From $(0, 2)$: right $1$, up $3$ lands on $(1, 5)$ — the $y$-value is $5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Just plug in
steps: Moving right $1$ from $x = 0$ puts you at $x = 1$.
$y = 3 \times 1 + 2 = 5$ — the graph move and the formula agree.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: Moving up by 1 — copying the run instead of the slope — lands on 3 instead of 5.
The slope 3 is the STAIR HEIGHT: right 1, up 3. From (0, 2) that is (1, 5), so y = 5.

prompt: The line $y = 4x - 8$ crosses the $x$-axis where $y = 0$. What is $x$ there?
hint: Set $y = 0$: solve $0 = 4x - 8$.

hints.text: Set $y = 0$: solve $0 = 4x - 8$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Simpler: $y = 2x - 4$ hits zero when $2x = 4$, so $x = 2$. Set your $y$ to $0$ and solve the same way.
Add $8$ to both sides: $8 = 4x$. Then divide.

explanation: Divide by $4$: $x = 2$. The line crosses at $(2, 0)$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Climb from the start
steps: The line starts at $(0, -8)$, which is $8$ below the $x$-axis, and climbs $4$ per step.
It needs $8 \div 4 = 2$ steps to reach height $0$ — so it crosses at $x = 2$.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: −8 is the y-intercept — where the line crosses the OTHER axis — and it is the classic mix-up here.
Crossing the x-axis means y = 0: solve 4x − 8 = 0 to get x = 2. Which axis you cross decides which letter is zero.

prompt: A line has slope $5$ and $y$-intercept $1$. Write its equation in the form $y = mx + b$.
hint: In $y = mx + b$, drop the slope into the $m$ spot and the intercept into the $b$ spot.

hints.text: In $y = mx + b$, drop the slope into the $m$ spot and the intercept into the $b$ spot.
$m = 5$ and $b = 1$: $y = 5x + \underline{\ \ }$.

explanation: Slope $m = 5$ goes in front of $x$; intercept $b = 1$ is added at the end.

alternativeExplanations.title: Start-then-move story
steps: The intercept is where you START: height $1$ on the $y$-axis.
The slope is how you MOVE: up $5$ per step across.
Start $1$, move $5x$: $y = 5x + 1$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Build the table first
steps: Start at $x = 0, y = 1$ and jump $5$ each step: $0 \to 1$, $1 \to 6$, $2 \to 11$.
Jump $5$ means $5x$; the value at zero, $1$, is the $+b$: $y = 5x + 1$.

prompt: You start with $\$15$ saved and add $\$5$ every week. Write an equation for your savings $y$ after $x$ weeks.
hint: Find the START (money at week $0$) and the MOVE (money added per week).

hints.text: Find the START (money at week $0$) and the MOVE (money added per week).
Start $b = 15$, move $m = 5$ per week. Fill in $y = mx + b$.

explanation: The start is $b = 15$ — the money before any weeks pass.
The move is $m = 5$ — dollars added each week.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test it on a week
steps: After $2$ weeks you should have $15 + 5 + 5 = 25$ dollars.
The equation says $y = 5 \times 2 + 15 = 25$. It matches, so it is right.

alternativeExplanations.title: From a table
steps: Week $0 \to 15$, week $1 \to 20$, week $2 \to 25$: a steady jump of $+5$.
The jump is $m = 5$; the week-zero value $15$ is $b$: $y = 5x + 15$.

prompt: A table shows $x: 0, 1, 2$ and $y: 7, 10, 13$. What is $b$, the starting value of the line?
hint: $b$ is the $y$-value when $x = 0$ — the START.

hints.text: $b$ is the $y$-value when $x = 0$ — the START.
Look at the first column of the table: $x = 0$ pairs with which $y$?

explanation: So $b = 7$. (The jump of $+3$ each step is $m$, but that is not what was asked.)

alternativeExplanations.title: On the graph
steps: The point on the $y$-axis is $(0, 7)$ — the line starts at height $7$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Walk the pattern backward
steps: The $y$-values climb by $3$: $7, 10, 13$.
Step back from $x = 1$: $10 - 3 = 7$ at $x = 0$ — the start is $7$.

prompt: A table shows $x: 1, 2, 3$ and $y: 9, 13, 17$. The $y$-values jump by the same amount each step. What is the slope $m$?
hint: The slope is the constant JUMP in $y$ each time $x$ grows by $1$.

hints.text: The slope is the constant JUMP in $y$ each time $x$ grows by $1$.
From $9$ to $13$ is a jump of how much? Check $13$ to $17$ too.
Both jumps are $4$, so $m = 4$.

explanation: $x$ climbs by $1$ each column, and $y$ climbs $9 \to 13 \to 17$.
A constant jump of $4$ per step means slope $m = 4$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Slope formula
steps: Take two rows as points: $(1, 9)$ and $(3, 17)$.
$m = \frac{17 - 9}{3 - 1} = \frac{8}{2} = 4$ — same answer as the jump.

alternativeExplanations.title: Rate story
steps: Read the table as pay: hour $1 \to \$9$, hour $2 \to \$13$, hour $3 \to \$17$.
You earn $\$4$ more every hour — that per-hour rate is the slope, $4$.

prompt: A gym charges a $\$25$ sign-up fee plus $\$10$ per month. Write an equation for the total cost $y$ after $x$ months.
hint: The one-time fee is the START ($b$); the monthly charge is the MOVE ($m$).

hints.text: The one-time fee is the START ($b$); the monthly charge is the MOVE ($m$).
$b = 25$, $m = 10$. Fill in $y = mx + b$.

explanation: At $0$ months you already owe the sign-up fee: $b = 25$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check with 3 months
steps: Three months should cost $25 + 10 + 10 + 10 = \$55$.
The equation gives $10 \times 3 + 25 = 55$ — it checks out.

alternativeExplanations.title: Table of bills
steps: Month $0 \to 25$, month $1 \to 35$, month $2 \to 45$: constant jump $+10$.
Jump $10$ is $m$; month-zero bill $25$ is $b$: $y = 10x + 25$.

prompt: A candle starts $20$ cm tall and burns $2$ cm every hour. Write an equation for its height $h$ after $t$ hours.
hint: The height goes DOWN, so the rate is negative: $-2$ cm per hour.

hints.text: The height goes DOWN, so the rate is negative: $-2$ cm per hour.
Start at $20$, subtract $2$ for each hour: $h = 20 - \underline{\ \ }t$.

explanation: Move: the candle LOSES $2$ cm per hour, so $m = -2$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check an hour
steps: After $3$ hours the candle burned $3 \times 2 = 6$ cm, leaving $20 - 6 = 14$ cm.
The equation gives $h = 20 - 2 \times 3 = 14$ — it matches.

alternativeExplanations.title: Downhill stairs table
steps: Hour $0 \to 20$, hour $1 \to 18$, hour $2 \to 16$: a steady jump of $-2$.
Jump $-2$ is the slope, start $20$ is $b$: $h = -2t + 20$, the same as $20 - 2t$.

prompt: A table shows $x: 0, 1, 2$ and $y: 3, 8, 13$. Write the equation of the line in the form $y = mx + b$.
hint: Two jobs: find the constant JUMP (that is $m$), then the value at $x = 0$ (that is $b$).

hints.text: Two jobs: find the constant JUMP (that is $m$), then the value at $x = 0$ (that is $b$).
Jump: $8 - 3 = 5$. Start: $y = 3$ when $x = 0$.

explanation: The jump: $3 \to 8 \to 13$ climbs by $5$ each step, so $m = 5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Machine story
steps: Think of a machine: input $x$, and the output starts at $3$ then adds $5$ per input step.
"Times 5, plus 3" in machine language is $y = 5x + 3$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Slope formula on two rows
steps: The row $(0, 3)$ hands you $b = 3$ directly: $y = 5x + 3$.

prompt: A line passes through $(0, 6)$ and $(2, 12)$. Write its equation in the form $y = mx + b$.
hint: Slope first: $m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$. Then notice one point has $x = 0$.

hints.text: Slope first: $m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$. Then notice one point has $x = 0$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Easier pair: $(0, 1)$ and $(2, 5)$ rise $4$ over run $2$, so $m = 2$ and $b = 1$: $y = 2x + 1$. The $b$ is free when one point has $x = 0$.
$m = \frac{12 - 6}{2 - 0} = 3$. The point $(0, 6)$ IS the $y$-intercept.

explanation: A point with $x = 0$ gives $b$ for free: $b = 6$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Growth story
steps: Read the points as a plant: $6$ cm at week $0$, $12$ cm at week $2$.
It grew $6$ cm in $2$ weeks — $3$ cm per week from a $6$ cm start: $y = 3x + 6$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Fill in the table
steps: Between $x = 0$ and $x = 2$, $y$ goes $6 \to ? \to 12$; the middle must be $9$.
Jump $+3$ per step and start $6$: $y = 3x + 6$.

prompt: At sunrise the temperature is $55^\circ$ and it rises $3^\circ$ every hour. Write an equation for the temperature $y$ after $x$ hours.
hint: Sunrise is hour $0$ — that temperature is your START, $b$.

hints.text: Sunrise is hour $0$ — that temperature is your START, $b$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Check hour $1$: $55 + 3 = 58$ degrees. The starting temperature is $b$ and the hourly rise is $m$.
$b = 55$ and the MOVE is $+3$ per hour, so $m = 3$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check at noon-ish
steps: After $4$ hours it should be $55 + 3 \times 4 = 67$ degrees.
Counting by threes from $55$: $58, 61, 64, 67$ — the equation agrees.

alternativeExplanations.title: Table of hours
steps: Hour $0 \to 55$, hour $1 \to 58$, hour $2 \to 61$: constant jump $+3$.
Jump $3$ is $m$, hour-zero value $55$ is $b$: $y = 3x + 55$.

prompt: A line passes through $(1, 5)$ and $(3, 11)$. Write its equation in the form $y = mx + b$.
hint: Step 1: slope from the two points. Step 2: plug one point into $y = 3x + b$ to find $b$.

hints.text: Step 1: slope from the two points. Step 2: plug one point into $y = 3x + b$ to find $b$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with $(1, 3)$ and $(2, 5)$: slope $= 2$, then back-solve $3 = 2(1) + b$ to get $b = 1$. Find $m$ first, then hunt for $b$.

explanation: Find $b$ with the point $(1, 5)$: $5 = 3 \times 1 + b$, so $b = 2$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Walk back to the start
steps: The slope is $3$, so stepping LEFT one unit drops $y$ by $3$.
From $(1, 5)$, step back to $x = 0$: $y = 5 - 3 = 2$. That start is $b$: $y = 3x + 2$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Table with a gap
steps: Rows: $x = 1 \to 5$, $x = 2 \to ?$, $x = 3 \to 11$; the jump must be $3$, so the middle is $8$.
Extend back to $x = 0$: $5 - 3 = 2$. Jump $3$, start $2$: $y = 3x + 2$.

prompt: Two rules must BOTH be true: $y = x + 3$ and $y = 2x$. What is $x$?
hint: Both rules give the same $y$, so the right sides must match: set $x + 3 = 2x$.

hints.text: Both rules give the same $y$, so the right sides must match: set $x + 3 = 2x$.
Subtract $x$ from both sides of $x + 3 = 2x$ to get $3 = x$.
$x = 3$. Check: $y = 3 + 3 = 6$ and $y = 2 \times 3 = 6$. Both rules agree.

explanation: A system is two rules that must both be true at once — the point where two lines cross.
Since both equal $y$, set them equal: $x + 3 = 2x$.
Subtract $x$: $3 = x$. Check: both rules give $y = 6$. ✓

alternativeExplanations.title: Build a table
steps: Try x-values in both rules. x = 1: rule one gives 4, rule two gives 2. x = 2: gives 5 and 4.
x = 3: gives 6 and 6 — a match! The rules agree at x = 3.

alternativeExplanations.title: As two racers
steps: Racer one starts 3 steps ahead and moves 1 step per turn (y = x + 3). Racer two starts at 0 but moves 2 steps per turn (y = 2x).
Racer two closes the 3-step gap by 1 step each turn, so they meet after 3 turns: x = 3.

prompt: Solve the system by substitution: $y = x + 1$ and $x + y = 9$. What is $x$?
hint: Substitution means "swap in what $y$ equals." Replace $y$ in the second equation with $x + 1$.

hints.text: Substitution means "swap in what $y$ equals." Replace $y$ in the second equation with $x + 1$.
That gives $x + (x + 1) = 9$, so $2x + 1 = 9$.

explanation: The first rule tells you exactly what $y$ is: $x + 1$. Swap that in for $y$ in the second rule.

alternativeExplanations.title: Think in words
steps: Two numbers add to 9, and one of them is exactly 1 bigger than the other.
Split 9 into two nearly-equal parts: 4 and 5. The smaller one is x, so x = 4.

alternativeExplanations.title: Guess and check with a table
steps: Try x = 3: then y = 4 and x + y = 7. Too small. Try x = 5: then y = 6 and x + y = 11. Too big.
Try x = 4: then y = 5 and 4 + 5 = 9. Just right, so x = 4.

prompt: A shelter has 12 pets total, all cats and dogs. There are 4 more cats than dogs. How many cats are there?
hint: Write two rules: $c + d = 12$ and $c = d + 4$.

hints.text: Write two rules: $c + d = 12$ and $c = d + 4$.
Swap in what $c$ equals: $(d + 4) + d = 12$, so $2d + 4 = 12$.
$2d = 8$, so $d = 4$ dogs and $c = 4 + 4 = 8$ cats.

explanation: Two rules must both be true: cats plus dogs is 12, and cats are 4 more than dogs.

alternativeExplanations.title: Share it out evenly first
steps: Split 12 pets evenly: 6 cats and 6 dogs. But cats need to be 4 MORE than dogs.
Move 2 pets from the dog pile to the cat pile: 8 cats and 4 dogs. Now the gap is 4. Cats = 8.

alternativeExplanations.title: Take away the extra
steps: Set the 4 extra cats aside. The remaining 12 − 4 = 8 pets split evenly: 4 cats and 4 dogs.
Give the 4 extras back to the cats: 4 + 4 = 8 cats.

prompt: Plan A costs $\$20$ plus $\$5$ per month. Plan B costs $\$10$ plus $\$7$ per month. After how many months do they cost the same?
hint: Set the two costs equal: $20 + 5m = 10 + 7m$.

hints.text: Set the two costs equal: $20 + 5m = 10 + 7m$.
Subtract $5m$ and $10$ from both sides: $10 = 2m$.
$m = 10 \div 2 = 5$ months.

explanation: $m = 5$. Check: both plans cost $\$45$ at 5 months. ✓

alternativeExplanations.title: Build a table
steps: Month 1: A = 25, B = 17. Month 3: A = 35, B = 31. B is catching up by $2 each month.
A starts $10 ahead and B gains $2 per month: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 months to tie.

alternativeExplanations.title: As two racers
steps: Plan A starts 10 dollars ahead but walks 5 per month; B runs 7 per month.
B closes the 10-dollar gap at 2 per month → catches A after 5 months.

prompt: Solve by substitution: $y = 2x - 1$ and $3x + y = 14$. What is $x$?
hint: Swap in what $y$ equals: replace $y$ in $3x + y = 14$ with $2x - 1$.

hints.text: Swap in what $y$ equals: replace $y$ in $3x + y = 14$ with $2x - 1$.

explanation: The first rule hands you $y$ on a plate: $y = 2x - 1$. Swap it into the second rule.

alternativeExplanations.title: Guess and check with a table
steps: Try x = 2: y = 3 and 3(2) + 3 = 9. Too small. Try x = 4: y = 7 and 12 + 7 = 19. Too big.
Try x = 3: y = 5 and 9 + 5 = 14. That is it — x = 3.

alternativeExplanations.title: Picture the swap
steps: Think of y as a labeled box. The label says "2x − 1 lives inside."
The second equation 3x + [box] = 14 becomes 3x + 2x − 1 = 14, which is 5 copies of x minus 1. Five copies make 15, so each copy is 3.

prompt: Solve by elimination: $x + y = 10$ and $x - y = 4$. What is $x$?
hint: Stack the equations and add them. The $+y$ and $-y$ cancel out.

hints.text: Stack the equations and add them. The $+y$ and $-y$ cancel out.
Adding gives $2x = 14$.

explanation: Elimination means "stack and cancel." Stack the two equations and add straight down.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sum and difference story
steps: Two numbers add to 10 and are 4 apart. The bigger one sits half the gap above the middle.
The middle of 10 is 5, and half of 4 is 2. Bigger number: 5 + 2 = 7. So x = 7.

alternativeExplanations.title: Build a table
steps: List pairs that add to 10: (6, 4), (7, 3), (8, 2).
Which pair is 4 apart? 7 − 3 = 4. So x = 7 and y = 3.

prompt: At a school play, 3 adult tickets and 2 kid tickets cost $\$41$. One adult ticket and 2 kid tickets cost $\$23$. How many dollars does one adult ticket cost?
hint: Both orders have the SAME 2 kid tickets. Stack the equations and subtract to cancel the kids.

hints.text: Both orders have the SAME 2 kid tickets. Stack the equations and subtract to cancel the kids.
$a = 18 \div 2 = 9$ dollars per adult ticket.

explanation: Both have $2k$, so subtract the second from the first — the kid tickets cancel: $2a = 18$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Compare the two receipts
steps: The big order is the small order plus 2 extra adult tickets. The price difference is 41 − 23 = 18 dollars.
So 2 adult tickets cost $18, and one costs 18 ÷ 2 = 9 dollars.

alternativeExplanations.title: Picture the ticket piles
steps: Draw both orders: [A A A K K] = 41 and [A K K] = 23.
Cross off one A and two Ks from each pile. What is left is [A A] = 18, so each A is 9.

prompt: Solve the system: $2x + 3y = 19$ and $x + y = 8$. What is $y$?
hint: The $x$s do not match yet. Multiply the whole second equation by 2 to get $2x + 2y = 16$.

hints.text: The $x$s do not match yet. Multiply the whole second equation by 2 to get $2x + 2y = 16$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Simpler system: $x + y = 5$ and $x = 3$ gives $y = 2$. Here, rewrite $x + y = 8$ as $x = 8 - y$ and swap it in.
Now stack and subtract: $(2x + 3y) - (2x + 2y) = 19 - 16$.
The $x$s cancel: $y = 3$. (And $x = 5$.)

explanation: To cancel with elimination, the copies must match. Double the second equation: $2x + 2y = 16$.
Subtract it from the first: the $2x$s vanish and $3y - 2y = y$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Substitution instead
steps: From x + y = 8, we know x = 8 − y. Swap that into the first rule: 2(8 − y) + 3y = 19.
That is 16 − 2y + 3y = 19, so 16 + y = 19 and y = 3.

alternativeExplanations.title: Guess pairs from the easy rule
steps: Pairs that add to 8: (5, 3), (4, 4), (6, 2). Test each in 2x + 3y = 19.
(5, 3) gives 10 + 9 = 19. It works, so y = 3.

prompt: A streaming service charges a $\$12$ sign-up fee plus $\$8$ per month. A rival charges no fee but $\$10$ per month. After how many months have you paid the same total on both?
hint: Write both totals: $12 + 8m$ and $10m$. Set them equal.

hints.text: Write both totals: $12 + 8m$ and $10m$. Set them equal.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Test month $1$: $12 + 8 = \$20$ versus the rival. Keep testing months, or set both cost expressions equal.
$12 + 8m = 10m$. Subtract $8m$ from both sides: $12 = 2m$.
$m = 12 \div 2 = 6$ months. Both totals are $\$60$.

explanation: Total cost is where the two rules cross: $12 + 8m = 10m$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Gap-closing story
steps: The fee puts you $12 behind on service one from day zero. But each month it charges $2 LESS than the rival.
Saving $2 a month erases a $12 head start in 12 ÷ 2 = 6 months.

alternativeExplanations.title: Build a table
steps: Month 2: fee plan = 28, rival = 20. Month 4: 44 vs 40. Month 6: 60 vs 60.
The totals tie at month 6.

prompt: You have 15 coins, all nickels and dimes, worth $\$1.10$ total. How many nickels do you have?
hint: Two rules in cents: $n + d = 15$ coins and $5n + 10d = 110$ cents.

hints.text: Two rules in cents: $n + d = 15$ coins and $5n + 10d = 110$ cents.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try all-nickels first: $15$ nickels is only $\$0.75$ — too little by $\$0.35$. Every dime swap adds $\$0.05$, so count the swaps.
$5n = 40$, so $n = 8$ nickels. (And 7 dimes.)

explanation: Count rule: $n + d = 15$. Money rule in cents: $5n + 10d = 110$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Pretend they are all dimes
steps: If all 15 coins were dimes, you would have 150 cents — that is 40 cents too much.
Swapping a dime for a nickel drops the total by 5 cents. You need 40 ÷ 5 = 8 swaps, so 8 nickels.

alternativeExplanations.title: Build a table
steps: 10 nickels, 5 dimes: 50 + 50 = 100 cents. Too low. 6 nickels, 9 dimes: 30 + 90 = 120. Too high.
8 nickels, 7 dimes: 40 + 70 = 110 cents. That is the match — 8 nickels.

prompt: You fold a sheet of paper 5 times. Each fold doubles the layers, so you get $2^5$ layers. How many layers is that?
hint: $2^5$ means five copies of 2 multiplied: $2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2$.

hints.text: $2^5$ means five copies of 2 multiplied: $2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2$.
Double step by step: 2, 4, 8, 16, ...
One more double: $16 \times 2 = 32$ layers.

alternativeExplanations.title: Fold-by-fold table
steps: Fold 1: 2 layers. Fold 2: 4. Fold 3: 8. Fold 4: 16. Fold 5: 32.
Each row doubles the one before, so 5 folds give 32 layers.

prompt: Simplify: $x^3 \cdot x^4$. Write your answer as a power of $x$.
hint: $x^3$ is 3 copies of $x$, and $x^4$ is 4 more copies. Count ALL the copies.

hints.text: $x^3$ is 3 copies of $x$, and $x^4$ is 4 more copies. Count ALL the copies.
Multiplying powers with the same base ADDS the exponents: $x^{3+4}$.

explanation: $x^3 \cdot x^4$ means $(x \cdot x \cdot x)(x \cdot x \cdot x \cdot x)$ — copies of $x$ lined up.
So $x^3 \cdot x^4 = x^7$. Product rule: add the exponents.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test with real numbers
steps: Let x = 2. Then 2³ = 8 and 2⁴ = 16, and 8 × 16 = 128.
128 is 2⁷, not 2¹². So the exponents add: x⁷.

alternativeExplanations.title: Two boxes of copies
steps: Picture a box holding 3 x-tiles and a box holding 4 x-tiles, all being multiplied together.
Dump both boxes into one: 3 + 4 = 7 tiles, which is x⁷.

prompt: Evaluate: $5^3$.
hint: $5^3$ means three copies of 5 multiplied: $5 \times 5 \times 5$.

hints.text: $5^3$ means three copies of 5 multiplied: $5 \times 5 \times 5$.
First pair: $5 \times 5 = 25$. Now multiply by the last 5.

alternativeExplanations.title: Picture a cube
steps: 5³ counts the little blocks in a 5-by-5-by-5 cube.
One layer holds 5 × 5 = 25 blocks, and there are 5 layers: 25 × 5 = 125.

alternativeExplanations.title: Break 25 apart
steps: 25 × 5 is the same as (20 + 5) × 5.

prompt: Simplify: $x^8 \div x^3$. Write your answer as a power of $x$.
hint: Write it as a fraction: 8 copies of $x$ on top, 3 copies on the bottom.

hints.text: Write it as a fraction: 8 copies of $x$ on top, 3 copies on the bottom.
Each bottom copy cancels one top copy. How many top copies survive?
$8 - 3 = 5$ copies survive: $x^5$.

explanation: $\frac{x^8}{x^3}$ has 8 copies of $x$ upstairs and 3 downstairs.
Cancel the copies: each bottom $x$ wipes out one top $x$, three times.
That leaves $8 - 3 = 5$ copies: $x^5$. Quotient rule: subtract the exponents.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test with real numbers
steps: Let x = 2. Then 2⁸ = 256 and 2³ = 8, and 256 ÷ 8 = 32.
32 = 2⁵, so the exponents subtract: x⁵.

alternativeExplanations.title: Undo a multiplication
steps: Division undoes multiplication. Ask: x³ times WHAT gives x⁸?
Multiplying adds exponents, so you need 3 + ? = 8. The missing power is x⁵.

prompt: Simplify: $(x^2)^4$. Write your answer as a power of $x$.
hint: $(x^2)^4$ means four copies of $x^2$ multiplied: $x^2 \cdot x^2 \cdot x^2 \cdot x^2$.

hints.text: $(x^2)^4$ means four copies of $x^2$ multiplied: $x^2 \cdot x^2 \cdot x^2 \cdot x^2$.
Each $x^2$ carries 2 copies of $x$, and there are 4 groups: $2 \times 4$ copies.

explanation: A power of a power is copies of copies: 4 groups, each holding 2 copies of $x$.
So $(x^2)^4 = x^8$. Power rule: multiply the exponents.

alternativeExplanations.title: Add them up with the product rule
steps: Unroll it: (x²)⁴ = x² · x² · x² · x².
Multiplying powers adds exponents: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8, so x⁸.

alternativeExplanations.title: Egg-carton picture
steps: Picture 4 cartons, each holding 2 eggs. Every egg is one copy of x being multiplied.
Total eggs: 4 × 2 = 8, so the answer is x⁸.

prompt: A rumor spreads in rounds: each person tells exactly 3 new people. In round 4, the number of new people who hear it is $3^4$. How many people is that?
hint: $3^4$ means four copies of 3 multiplied: $3 \times 3 \times 3 \times 3$.

hints.text: $3^4$ means four copies of 3 multiplied: $3 \times 3 \times 3 \times 3$.
Triple step by step: 3, 9, 27, ...
One more triple: $27 \times 3 = 81$ people.

explanation: Each round multiplies by 3, so round 4 is $3^4 = 3 \times 3 \times 3 \times 3$.
81 new people hear the rumor in round 4.

alternativeExplanations.title: Round-by-round table
steps: Round 1: 3 people. Round 2: 9. Round 3: 27. Round 4: 81.
Each row is triple the last, so round 4 reaches 81 people.

prompt: A game power-up multiplies your score by $4^0$. What number does it multiply your score by?
hint: The exponent counts copies of 4 to multiply. Here there are ZERO copies.

hints.text: The exponent counts copies of 4 to multiply. Here there are ZERO copies.
Zero copies of multiplying leaves the do-nothing number for multiplication.
$4^0 = 1$. Your score is multiplied by 1 — it stays the same.

explanation: Zero copies of multiplying means you do nothing, and the do-nothing number for multiplication is 1.
So $4^0 = 1$, and your score does not change.

alternativeExplanations.title: Walk down the staircase
steps: 4³ = 64, 4² = 16, 4¹ = 4. Each step DOWN divides by 4.
One more step: 4⁰ = 4 ÷ 4 = 1.

alternativeExplanations.title: Use the quotient rule
steps: 4⁰ is the same as 4² ÷ 4², since 2 − 2 = 0.
But any number divided by itself is 1, so 4⁰ = 1.

prompt: Evaluate: $2^{-3}$. Write your answer as a fraction.
hint: A negative exponent means "flip it under 1": $2^{-3} = \frac{1}{2^3}$.

hints.text: A negative exponent means "flip it under 1": $2^{-3} = \frac{1}{2^3}$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with $2^{-1}$, which is $\frac{1}{2}$. A negative exponent flips the power under a $1$ — so $2^{-3}$ flips $2^3$.
Evaluate the bottom: $2^3 = 8$.

explanation: A negative exponent is not a negative number — it flips the power under 1.

alternativeExplanations.title: Walk down the staircase
steps: 2² = 4, 2¹ = 2, 2⁰ = 1. Each step down divides by 2.

alternativeExplanations.title: Use the quotient rule
steps: 2⁻³ is the same as 2¹ ÷ 2⁴, since 1 − 4 = −3.
That is 2/16 = 1/8.

prompt: Simplify: $(x^3)^2 \cdot x^4 \div x^5$. Write your answer as a power of $x$.
hint: Handle the power of a power first: $(x^3)^2 = x^{3 \times 2} = x^6$.

hints.text: Handle the power of a power first: $(x^3)^2 = x^{3 \times 2} = x^6$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Do one rule at a time. First $(x^3)^2 = x^6$ (multiply the exponents). Now it is just $x^6 \cdot x^4 \div x^5$.
Now multiply: $x^6 \cdot x^4 = x^{6+4} = x^{10}$. Then divide.

explanation: Power rule first: $(x^3)^2 = x^6$ — 2 groups of 3 copies.
Product rule: $x^6 \cdot x^4 = x^{10}$ — combine the copies.
Quotient rule: $x^{10} \div x^5 = x^5$ — cancel 5 copies. Answer: $x^5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: One running count of copies
steps: Count copies of x from left to right: the square of x³ gives 6 copies, then +4 more makes 10.
Dividing by x⁵ erases 5 copies: 10 − 5 = 5 copies left, so x⁵.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test with real numbers
steps: Let x = 2. (2³)² = 64, times 2⁴ = 16 gives 1024. Divide by 2⁵ = 32: 1024 ÷ 32 = 32.
32 = 2⁵, so the simplified form is x⁵.

prompt: You text a funny picture to 2 friends, and every person who gets it sends it to 2 new people. After 10 rounds, the round reaches $2^{10}$ people. How many people is that?
hint: $2^{10}$ is ten copies of 2 multiplied. Use a landmark: $2^5 = 32$.

hints.text: $2^{10}$ is ten copies of 2 multiplied. Use a landmark: $2^5 = 32$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Count one round at a time: round $1$ reaches $2$ people, round $2$ reaches $4$, round $3$ reaches $8$. Each round DOUBLES.
Product rule with numbers: $2^{10} = 2^5 \times 2^5 = 32 \times 32$.
$32 \times 32 = 1024$ people.

explanation: Each round doubles the reach, so round 10 is $2^{10}$.
Split it with the product rule: $2^{10} = 2^5 \cdot 2^5$ because $5 + 5 = 10$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Keep doubling a list
steps: The 10th number in the doubling list is 1024.

prompt: A pattern goes 3, 6, 12, 24, ... Each step multiplies by the same number. What is that growth factor?
hint: Divide any term by the one before it: $6 \div 3 = ?$

hints.text: Divide any term by the one before it: $6 \div 3 = ?$
$6 \div 3 = 2$, and $12 \div 6 = 2$ too. The multiplier repeats.
The growth factor is 2 — each step doubles.

explanation: Exponential patterns MULTIPLY by the same factor each step.

alternativeExplanations.title: Rule out adding
steps: If the pattern ADDED the same amount, the jumps would match: but 3→6 adds 3 while 6→12 adds 6.
The jumps grow, so it multiplies. Each term is exactly double the last: factor 2.

alternativeExplanations.title: Photocopier picture
steps: Imagine a copier set to "enlarge ×2." Feed in 3, get 6. Feed in 6, get 12. Feed in 12, get 24.
One machine setting explains every step: the factor is 2.

prompt: An account starts with 200 followers and gains 100 new followers every week — the same amount each time. How many followers after 3 weeks?
hint: Adding the same amount each step is LINEAR growth: start plus 100 per week.

hints.text: Adding the same amount each step is LINEAR growth: start plus 100 per week.
Total added in 3 weeks: $3 \times 100 = 300$.

explanation: Linear growth ADDS the same amount every step.

alternativeExplanations.title: Week-by-week table
steps: Week 1: 300. Week 2: 400. Week 3: 500.
Each row climbs by exactly 100 — a straight staircase to 500.

alternativeExplanations.title: Picture a straight ramp
steps: On a graph, linear growth is a straight line starting at 200 and rising 100 per week.
Three equal steps up from 200 lands at 500.

prompt: A dish starts with 5 bacteria, and the count doubles every hour. How many bacteria after 3 hours?
hint: Doubling is exponential: multiply by 2 each hour, three times.

hints.text: Doubling is exponential: multiply by 2 each hour, three times.
Hour 1: $5 \times 2 = 10$. Hour 2: $10 \times 2 = 20$.
Hour 3: $20 \times 2 = 40$ bacteria.

explanation: Exponential growth multiplies by the same factor each step: here, $\times 2$ every hour.

alternativeExplanations.title: Hour-by-hour table
steps: Hour 0: 5. Hour 1: 10. Hour 2: 20. Hour 3: 40.
Each row doubles the last — after 3 hours, 40 bacteria.

alternativeExplanations.title: Compare with adding
steps: If the dish ADDED 5 each hour (linear), 3 hours would give 5 + 15 = 20.
Doubling is faster: 5 × 8 = 40 — exponential growth pulls ahead.

prompt: A quantity grows by $10\%$ each year. What growth factor do you multiply by each year? (Write it as a decimal.)
hint: Growing 10% means you keep ALL of it (100%) plus 10% more.

hints.text: Growing 10% means you keep ALL of it (100%) plus 10% more.
$100\% + 10\% = 110\%$. Turn that percent into a decimal.
$110\% = 1.10$. Multiply by 1.10 each year.

explanation: "Up 10%" means the new amount is 110% of the old one.
So each year you multiply by the growth factor 1.10.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test it on $100
steps: Start with $100. Growing 10% adds $10, giving $110.
What times 100 gives 110? 110 ÷ 100 = 1.10 — that is the factor.

alternativeExplanations.title: Keep-plus-gain picture
steps: Picture the amount as a full bar (the 1) plus a small extra slice (the 0.10).
Keep + gain = 1 + 0.10 = 1.10 per year.

prompt: A quantity shrinks by $20\%$ each year. What factor do you multiply by each year? (Write it as a decimal.)
hint: Losing 20% means you KEEP the rest. What percent is left?

hints.text: Losing 20% means you KEEP the rest. What percent is left?
$100\% - 20\% = 80\%$. Turn that into a decimal.
$80\% = 0.80$. Multiply by 0.80 each year.

explanation: "Down 20%" means you keep $100\% - 20\% = 80\%$ of the amount.
So each year you multiply by 0.80. (Never multiply by 0.20 — that is what you LOSE.)

alternativeExplanations.title: Test it on $100
steps: Start with $100. Losing 20% takes away $20, leaving $80.
80 ÷ 100 = 0.80, so the yearly factor is 0.80.

alternativeExplanations.title: Pizza picture
steps: Cut the amount into 5 equal slices. Losing 20% means one slice disappears.
Four of five slices remain: 4/5 = 0.80 of the amount each year.

prompt: An exponential rule is $y = 3 \cdot 2^x$ (start 3, factor 2). What is $y$ when $x = 4$?
hint: Exponent first: $2^4 = ?$

hints.text: Exponent first: $2^4 = ?$
$2^4 = 16$. Now multiply by the start value 3.

explanation: $y = a \cdot b^x$ means start $\times$ factor, applied $x$ times.
Then $y = 3 \times 16 = 48$. (Not $6^4$ — never multiply the start into the base!)

alternativeExplanations.title: Double step by step
steps: Start at 3 and double 4 times: 3 → 6 → 12 → 24 → 48.
After 4 doublings, y = 48.

alternativeExplanations.title: Table of x and y
steps: Each row doubles, landing on 48 at x = 4.

prompt: Your phone is worth $\$500$ new and loses $20\%$ of its value each year. How many dollars is it worth after 2 years?
hint: Losing 20% means keeping 80%: multiply by 0.80 each year.

hints.text: Losing 20% means keeping 80%: multiply by 0.80 each year.
Year 1: $500 \times 0.80 = 400$. Now do year 2.
Year 2: $400 \times 0.80 = 320$ dollars.

explanation: Each year the phone keeps 80% of its value: factor 0.80.

alternativeExplanations.title: Year-by-year table
steps: Notice it loses $100 the first year but only $80 the second — decay shrinks by a factor, not a fixed amount.

alternativeExplanations.title: Slice off a fifth twice
steps: Losing 20% = losing one fifth. One fifth of 500 is 100, leaving 400.
One fifth of 400 is 80, leaving 320. Value: $320.

prompt: A magic penny starts at 1 cent and doubles in value every day. After 10 doublings, how many cents is it worth?
hint: Ten doublings means $1 \times 2^{10}$ cents.

hints.text: Ten doublings means $1 \times 2^{10}$ cents.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Shrink it: after $3$ doublings a penny is $1 \to 2 \to 4 \to 8$ cents, which is $2^3$. So $10$ doublings is $2^{10}$.
Use a landmark: $2^5 = 32$, and $2^{10} = 32 \times 32$.
$32 \times 32 = 1024$ cents (over ten dollars!).

explanation: Doubling is exponential: $y = 1 \cdot 2^x$ cents after $x$ doublings.
The penny is worth 1024 cents — more than $\$10$ from one cent.

alternativeExplanations.title: List the doubles
steps: Ten arrows, ten doublings: 1024 cents.

alternativeExplanations.title: Compare with $5 a day
steps: Adding $5 a day for 10 days gives $50 — but that pace never speeds up.
The doubling penny hits $10.24 by day 10 and would pass $5,000,000 by day 30. Multiplying beats adding in the long run.

prompt: Account A starts with 10 followers and DOUBLES every week. Account B starts with 10 and ADDS 100 every week. After how many weeks does A first have more followers than B?
hint: Track both: A is $10 \cdot 2^w$ and B is $10 + 100w$.

hints.text: Track both: A is $10 \cdot 2^w$ and B is $10 + 100w$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Fill two weeks: A goes $10 \to 20 \to 40$ while B goes $10 \to 20 \to 30$. Doubling starts slow, then rockets past adding.
Week 5: A $= 320$, B $= 510$. B still leads. Try week 6.
Week 6: A $= 640$, B $= 610$. A first passes B at week 6.

explanation: Linear B adds 100 each week; exponential A multiplies by 2.
A first passes B after 6 weeks. Exponential always wins eventually.

alternativeExplanations.title: Watch the weekly jumps
steps: B always jumps by exactly 100. A jumps by its whole current size: +160 in week 5, +320 in week 6.
Once A jumps more than 100 per week AND closes the gap, it takes the lead — that happens in week 6 (640 vs 610).

alternativeExplanations.title: Tortoise and rocket
steps: B is a tortoise on a moving walkway: steady +100, a straight line on a graph. A is a rocket: slow at launch, then curving up faster and faster.
The rocket lags for 5 weeks, then blasts past in week 6 and never looks back.

prompt: A town of 2000 people grows $10\%$ per year. How many people after 2 years?
hint: Up 10% means multiply by 1.10 each year — do NOT just add 200 twice.

hints.text: Up 10% means multiply by 1.10 each year — do NOT just add 200 twice.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: One year first: $10\%$ of $2000$ is $200$, so year one ends at $2200$. Now take $10\%$ of the NEW total, not the old one.
Year 1: $2000 \times 1.10 = 2200$. Now grow year 2 from 2200.
Year 2: $2200 \times 1.10 = 2420$ people.

explanation: That is 2420 people — more than $2000 + 200 + 200 = 2400$, because year 2 grows the NEW total.

alternativeExplanations.title: Year-by-year table
steps: Year 2 adds 10% of 2200 = 220 → 2420. The add-on grows each year.

alternativeExplanations.title: Interest on the interest
steps: Plain adding would give 2000 + 200 + 200 = 2400.
But the 200 newcomers from year 1 also grow 10% in year 2 — that extra 10% of 200 is 20 more, so 2400 + 20 = 2420.

prompt: Simplify $4x + 3x$.
hint: Both terms are $x$-terms — the same kind of sticker.

hints.text: Both terms are $x$-terms — the same kind of sticker.
Four $x$ stickers plus three $x$ stickers. Add the front numbers: $4 + 3$.

explanation: $4x$ and $3x$ are like terms — same variable part.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sticker sorting
steps: Picture 4 apple stickers and 3 more apple stickers — all the same kind.
Same kind means you can count them together: 7 apple stickers, so 7x.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test a value
steps: Try x = 2: then 4x + 3x = 8 + 6 = 14.
And 7x = 14 too — the shorter form gives the same value, so 7x is right.

hint: Sort the stickers: $x$-terms in one pile, plain numbers in another.

hints.text: Sort the stickers: $x$-terms in one pile, plain numbers in another.
$3x + 2x$ makes one pile, $4 + 5$ makes the other.
$3x + 2x = 5x$ and $4 + 5 = 9$, so the sum is $5x + 9$.

explanation: Adding polynomials means combining like terms.

alternativeExplanations.title: Two bags of blocks
steps: Bag one holds 3 long x-blocks and 4 unit cubes. Bag two holds 2 long blocks and 5 cubes.
Pour both bags out: 5 long blocks and 9 cubes total — that is 5x + 9.

alternativeExplanations.title: Stack them vertically
steps: Write 3x + 4 on top of 2x + 5, lining up x-terms over x-terms.
Add each column like column addition: 5x in the x column, 9 in the number column.

prompt: Multiply: $x(x + 5)$.
hint: The outside $x$ hands a snack to EVERYONE inside the parentheses.

hints.text: The outside $x$ hands a snack to EVERYONE inside the parentheses.
$x \times x = x^2$ and $x \times 5 = 5x$.

explanation: Distribute the outside $x$ to both terms inside.

alternativeExplanations.title: Area picture
steps: Draw a rectangle x tall and (x + 5) wide, split into two patches: one x wide, one 5 wide.
The patches have areas x·x = x² and x·5 = 5x. Total area: x² + 5x.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test a value
steps: Try x = 2: the original is 2(2 + 5) = 2 × 7 = 14.
The answer form gives 2² + 5·2 = 4 + 10 = 14. Same value — the multiplication is correct.

prompt: Subtract: $(5x + 7) - (2x + 3)$.
hint: The minus sign hits EVERY term in the second parentheses.

hints.text: The minus sign hits EVERY term in the second parentheses.
Rewrite it as $5x + 7 - 2x - 3$, then combine like terms.
$5x - 2x = 3x$ and $7 - 3 = 4$, so the answer is $3x + 4$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Take away stickers
steps: Start with 5 x-stickers and 7 dot-stickers.
Peel off 2 x-stickers and 3 dot-stickers — take BOTH kinds away.
You are left with 3 x-stickers and 4 dots: 3x + 4.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check with a value
steps: And 3x + 4 at x = 10 is 30 + 4 = 34. The forms match, so 3x + 4 is right.

prompt: Your phone case business brings in revenue of $3x^2 + 5x$ dollars and pays costs of $x^2 + 2x$ dollars. Write the profit: revenue minus cost.
hint: Profit means money in minus money out: $(3x^2 + 5x) - (x^2 + 2x)$.

hints.text: Profit means money in minus money out: $(3x^2 + 5x) - (x^2 + 2x)$.
The minus distributes: $3x^2 + 5x - x^2 - 2x$. Now match $x^2$ with $x^2$, and $x$ with $x$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Two sticker piles
steps: x²-terms are one kind of sticker, x-terms are another — never mix the piles.
x² pile: 3 minus 1 leaves 2, so 2x². x pile: 5 minus 2 leaves 3, so 3x.
Profit: 2x² + 3x.

alternativeExplanations.title: Try a sales number
steps: Say x = 10 cases. Revenue: 3(100) + 50 = 350 dollars. Cost: 100 + 20 = 120 dollars.
Profit: 350 − 120 = 230. Check the formula: 2(100) + 3(10) = 230. It works.

prompt: A rectangular garden is $(x + 3)$ meters long and $(x + 2)$ meters wide. Multiply to write its area.
hint: Split the garden into 4 patches: cut the length into $x$ and $3$, the width into $x$ and $2$.

hints.text: Split the garden into 4 patches: cut the length into $x$ and $3$, the width into $x$ and $2$.
The 4 patch areas are $x \times x$, $x \times 2$, $3 \times x$, and $3 \times 2$. Add them up.

explanation: Draw the area model: a rectangle split into 4 patches.

alternativeExplanations.title: Distribute twice
steps: Hand (x + 2) to each part of (x + 3): x(x + 2) + 3(x + 2).
That gives x² + 2x + 3x + 6.
Combine: x² + 5x + 6.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check with a real garden
steps: Let x = 5. Then the garden is 8 m by 7 m, area 56 square meters.
The formula: 5² + 5·5 + 6 = 25 + 25 + 6 = 56. The expanded form is correct.

prompt: Multiply: $2x(3x + 4)$.
hint: The $2x$ outside hands a snack to BOTH terms inside.

hints.text: The $2x$ outside hands a snack to BOTH terms inside.
$2x \times 3x = 6x^2$ (multiply numbers, multiply the $x$s).
$2x \times 3x = 6x^2$ and $2x \times 4 = 8x$, so the answer is $6x^2 + 8x$.

explanation: $2x \times 3x = 6x^2$ — the coefficients multiply and $x \times x = x^2$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Area picture
steps: Draw a rectangle 2x tall and (3x + 4) wide, cut into two patches.
Left patch: 2x by 3x, area 6x². Right patch: 2x by 4, area 8x.
Total: 6x² + 8x.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test a value
steps: Try x = 1: the original is 2(3 + 4) = 14.
The answer gives 6 + 8 = 14 — same number, so the distribution worked.

prompt: Multiply $(x + 5)(x + 2)$. What is the coefficient of the $x$ term in the result?
hint: Use the area model: 4 patches. Two of them are $x$-patches.

hints.text: Use the area model: 4 patches. Two of them are $x$-patches.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try $(x + 1)(x + 2)$: the middle terms are $2x + 1x = 3x$. The x-coefficient is just the two numbers ADDED.
The $x$-patches are $2 \times x$ and $5 \times x$. Add them.
$2x + 5x = 7x$, so the coefficient is $7$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Garden patches
steps: A garden (x + 5) by (x + 2) splits into 4 patches: a square x by x, a 2-by-x strip, a 5-by-x strip, and a 5-by-2 corner.
The two strips are the x-terms: 2x and 5x, which is 7x together. Coefficient: 7.

alternativeExplanations.title: Shortcut for this pattern
steps: For (x + a)(x + b), the middle coefficient is always a + b.
Here a = 5 and b = 2, so the x coefficient is 5 + 2 = 7.
